# List (/docs/galactik/display/list)

An accessible list of selectable rows built on @angular/aria/listbox, with composable slots for content lists, action menus and navigation lists.



`List` is a container of selectable rows built on `@angular/aria/listbox` (`role="listbox"`/`role="option"`).
`ListItem` is a row, and a set of slot components/directives (`ListItemText`, `ListItemLeft`, `ListItemIcon`,
`ListItemAvatar`, `ListItemAction`, `ListItemChevron`, `ListItemExpander`) compose the row content for content
lists, action menus, navigation lists and tree-style rows. A row can also carry one **action** (typically
a delete) that a keyboard user reaches with a key rather than with Tab — see
[Row action and its key](#row-action-and-its-key).

## Minimal example [#minimal-example]

<CodeSample id="list-basic" title="A single-selection list">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component, signal } from "@angular/core";
    import {
      ListComponent,
      ListItemComponent,
      ListItemLeftDirective,
      ListItemIconDirective,
      ListItemTextComponent,
      FileIcon,
      ImageIcon,
      UserIcon,
    } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [ListComponent, ListItemComponent, ListItemLeftDirective, ListItemIconDirective, ListItemTextComponent, FileIcon, ImageIcon, UserIcon],
      template: `
        <List class="gap-(--spacing-3xs)" [(value)]="picked">
          <ListItem value="doc">
            <ListItemLeft><ListItemIcon><file-icon /></ListItemIcon><ListItemText>Documents</ListItemText></ListItemLeft>
          </ListItem>
          <ListItem value="img">
            <ListItemLeft><ListItemIcon><image-icon /></ListItemIcon><ListItemText>Images</ListItemText></ListItemLeft>
          </ListItem>
          <ListItem value="ppl">
            <ListItemLeft><ListItemIcon><user-icon /></ListItemIcon><ListItemText>People</ListItemText></ListItemLeft>
          </ListItem>
        </List>
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      // `value` is always a V[] model, even for single selection.
      picked = signal<string[]>(["doc"]);
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

## How it works [#how-it-works]

`List` composes `@angular/aria/listbox`'s `Listbox` as a **host directive** on its own host element (not a
wrapper), and `ListItem` composes `Option` the same way — required so a projected `ListItem` resolves its
ancestor `Listbox` through the element-injector hierarchy, which an `ng-content` wrapper would break. Every
selection, keyboard-navigation and ARIA-reflection concern (`aria-selected`, `aria-disabled`, roving tabindex,
typeahead) comes from `@angular/aria`, not from galactik.

<Mermaid
  chart="flowchart TD
    List[&#x22;List (host-directive: Listbox, role=listbox)&#x22;]
    Item[&#x22;ListItem (host-directive: Option, role=option)&#x22;]
    Left[&#x22;ListItemLeft&#x22;]
    Text[&#x22;ListItemText (label + subtext)&#x22;]
    Action[&#x22;ListItemAction&#x22;]

    List -->|&#x22;variant()/size() defaults via LIST_REF&#x22;| Item
    Item --> Left
    Left --> Text
    Item --> Action

    User((&#x22;User&#x22;)) -- &#x22;click / arrow keys / typeahead&#x22; --> List
    User -- &#x22;the action's key (Delete by default)&#x22; --> Item
    List -- &#x22;aria-selected reflected on Option&#x22; --> Item
    List -- &#x22;[(value)] selection model&#x22; --> Consumer[[&#x22;Host component&#x22;]]
    Item -- &#x22;trigger()&#x22; --> Action
    Action -- &#x22;(click), stopPropagation()&#x22; --> Consumer"
/>

By default, `selectionMode="follow"` means moving keyboard focus (arrow keys) immediately changes the
selection — the listbox default. Set `selectionMode="explicit"` (paired with `multi`, typically) whenever a
row also carries its own interactive affordance like `ListItemAction`, since "select on focus" would otherwise
fight with reaching that action.

### Row action and its key [#row-action-and-its-key]

A `ListItemAction` is **not focusable**: its host `ListItem` is a listbox `option`, and ARIA forbids an option from
containing an interactive control. A mouse user clicks the icon, which appears on hover. A keyboard user presses
the action's key while the row has focus, and `ListItem` calls the action's `trigger()` — your `(click)` handler
fires exactly as it would for a click.

That key is declared on the action (`keys`, `Delete` by default) and made discoverable in three ways, because no
single one reaches everybody:

* **`aria-keyshortcuts`** on the row, set from `keys`;
* **a sentence** (`description`), rendered visually hidden and linked to the row by `aria-describedby`, so a
  screen reader reads it when the row takes focus. `aria-keyshortcuts` alone is not reliably read: it depends on
  the reader and its settings, and is then the raw key name, in English;
* **a second line in the row** (only when `description` is set), shown only while the row has *keyboard* focus (`:focus-visible`): the same
  sentence with the key set apart as a keycap. It is hidden otherwise — the mouse has the click, and showing it
  on hover would move the rows under the pointer. The row grows by that one line, and its trailing tag and action
  stay vertically centred on it. The rows below move down by that height while the row is focused, and back up
  when the focus leaves: reserving the space, overlaying the line and animating the height were tried and look
  worse, so the shift is accepted.

Both visible and hidden copies are `aria-hidden` or kept out of the option's name, so nothing is announced twice.
A disabled action promises nothing: no key, no sentence, no line.

## Recipes [#recipes]

### Multi-selection with a per-row action [#multi-selection-with-a-per-row-action]

<CodeSample id="list-multi-action" title="Explicit selection, with a trailing remove action">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component, signal } from "@angular/core";
    import {
      ListComponent,
      ListItemComponent,
      ListItemLeftDirective,
      ListItemAvatarDirective,
      ListItemTextComponent,
      ListItemActionComponent,
      XMarkIcon,
    } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    interface User {
      id: string;
      name: string;
      email: string;
      initials: string;
    }

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [ListComponent, ListItemComponent, ListItemLeftDirective, ListItemAvatarDirective, ListItemTextComponent, ListItemActionComponent, XMarkIcon],
      template: `
        <List class="gap-(--spacing-3xs)" multi size="medium" selectionMode="explicit" [(value)]="picked">
          @for (u of users(); track u.id) {
            <ListItem [value]="u.id">
              <ListItemLeft>
                <ListItemAvatar>{{ u.initials }}</ListItemAvatar>
                <ListItemText [subtext]="u.email">{{ u.name }}</ListItemText>
              </ListItemLeft>
              <ListItemAction ariaLabel="Remove" (click)="remove(u.id, $event)"><x-mark-icon /></ListItemAction>
            </ListItem>
          }
        </List>
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      users = signal<User[]>([
        { id: "ada", name: "Ada Lovelace", email: "ada@example.com", initials: "AL" },
        { id: "alan", name: "Alan Turing", email: "alan@example.com", initials: "AT" },
      ]);
      picked = signal<string[]>(["alan"]);

      remove(id: string, event: Event): void {
        event.stopPropagation(); // do not toggle the row's selection while removing it
        this.users.update((list) => list.filter((u) => u.id !== id));
        this.picked.update((p) => p.filter((v) => v !== id));
      }
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

### Name the key of a row action [#name-the-key-of-a-row-action]

Galactik has no translation layer: the sentence and the key's name are yours to provide. `description` must
contain `shortcut` as is for the key to be set apart as a keycap inside it. A key that only exists on some
keyboards is the caller's to add — a MacBook has no dedicated `Delete` (it is `fn+⌫`, and `⌫` alone emits
`Backspace`), so declare both there. `isApplePlatform()` is exported for that.

<CodeSample id="list-action-key" title="A delete action with a translated, announced key">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component, signal } from "@angular/core";
    import { isApplePlatform, ListComponent, ListItemComponent, ListItemTextComponent, ListItemActionComponent, XMarkIcon } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [ListComponent, ListItemComponent, ListItemTextComponent, ListItemActionComponent, XMarkIcon],
      template: `
        <List aria-label="Recent searches" size="medium" selectionMode="explicit">
          @for (search of searches(); track search) {
            <ListItem [value]="search">
              <ListItemText>{{ search }}</ListItemText>
              <ListItemAction
                ariaLabel="Remove"
                [keys]="deleteKeys"
                shortcut="Del"
                description="Press Del to delete"
                (click)="remove(search, $event)">
                <x-mark-icon />
              </ListItemAction>
            </ListItem>
          }
        </List>
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      searches = signal(["annual report", "contract template", "onboarding"]);

      // `Delete` everywhere, plus `Backspace` on a Mac, whose keyboard has no dedicated `Delete`.
      protected readonly deleteKeys = isApplePlatform() ? ["Delete", "Backspace"] : ["Delete"];

      remove(search: string, event: Event): void {
        event.stopPropagation(); // do not toggle the row's selection while removing it
        this.searches.update((list) => list.filter((s) => s !== search));
      }
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

The action does not have to be a delete: `keys` takes any `KeyboardEvent.key` values (`["Enter"]`, `["F2"]`…),
and the first one names the action in `aria-keyshortcuts`. There is still **one action per row**: `ListItem`
triggers the first `ListItemAction` it projects.

### Another icon, another key [#another-icon-another-key]

The icon is projected content and the key is `keys`, so an action is not a delete unless you make it one. Here
a rename: a pencil, answering to `F2` (the key file managers use). What the action *does* is whatever your
`(click)` handler does — the key only calls it.

<CodeSample id="list-action-rename" title="A rename action on F2, with its own icon and sentence">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component, signal } from "@angular/core";
    import { EditIcon, ListComponent, ListItemActionComponent, ListItemComponent, ListItemTextComponent } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [ListComponent, ListItemComponent, ListItemTextComponent, ListItemActionComponent, EditIcon],
      template: `
        <List aria-label="Documents" size="medium" selectionMode="explicit">
          @for (name of names(); track name) {
            <ListItem [value]="name">
              <ListItemText>{{ name }}</ListItemText>
              <ListItemAction
                ariaLabel="Rename"
                [keys]="['F2']"
                shortcut="F2"
                description="Press F2 to rename"
                (click)="rename(name, $event)">
                <edit-icon />
              </ListItemAction>
            </ListItem>
          }
        </List>
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      names = signal(["Annual report", "Contract template"]);

      rename(name: string, event: Event): void {
        event.stopPropagation(); // do not toggle the row's selection
        const next = window.prompt("New name", name);
        if (next) this.names.update((list) => list.map((n) => (n === name ? next : n)));
      }
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

The hover colour is part of the row, not of the action: every `ListItemAction` turns to the error colour on keyboard
focus and when hovered, since the delete is its main use. There is no `class` input to change that, and an icon
is the only thing you control. If an action needs its own look, or several actions side by side, it is not a
`ListItemAction` — see [Limits](#limits).

### Show a hint while the keyboard is in the list [#show-a-hint-while-the-keyboard-is-in-the-list]

A list is a single tab stop and the arrow keys do the rest, which nothing tells a keyboard user.
`List.keyboardFocused` is true while the keyboard focus — `:focus-visible`, so not a mouse click — is inside the
list, which is exactly when a hint is useful. Read it through the `list` template reference.

<CodeSample id="list-keyboard-hint" title="A navigation hint shown only to the keyboard">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component } from "@angular/core";
    import { KbdComponent, ListComponent, ListItemComponent, ListItemTextComponent } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [ListComponent, ListItemComponent, ListItemTextComponent, KbdComponent],
      template: `
        <List #list="list" aria-label="Documents" size="medium">
          <ListItem value="a"><ListItemText>Annual report</ListItemText></ListItem>
          <ListItem value="b"><ListItemText>Contract template</ListItemText></ListItem>
        </List>
        <!-- aria-hidden: a listbox already announces its arrow-key navigation to a screen reader -->
        @if (list.keyboardFocused()) {
          <p aria-hidden="true"><kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> to navigate</p>
        }
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {}
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

### Tree rows [#tree-rows]

`depth` indents a row by 20px per level, and `ListItemExpander` renders the rotating expand/collapse chevron.
In today's listbox-backed `List`, tree behavior is **style only** — expansion state and which children render
is entirely up to the consumer; there is no `role="tree"` keyboard semantics yet (a future
`@angular/aria/tree`-backed variant will add it).

<CodeSample id="list-tree" title="A collapsible folder row">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component, signal } from "@angular/core";
    import {
      ListComponent,
      ListItemComponent,
      ListItemLeftDirective,
      ListItemIconDirective,
      ListItemTextComponent,
      ListItemExpanderComponent,
      FolderIcon,
      FileIcon,
    } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [ListComponent, ListItemComponent, ListItemLeftDirective, ListItemIconDirective, ListItemTextComponent, ListItemExpanderComponent, FolderIcon, FileIcon],
      template: `
        <List [(value)]="picked">
          <ListItem value="src">
            <ListItemExpander [expanded]="open()" ariaLabel="Toggle" (click)="toggle($event)" />
            <ListItemLeft><ListItemIcon><folder-icon /></ListItemIcon><ListItemText>src</ListItemText></ListItemLeft>
          </ListItem>
          @if (open()) {
            <ListItem value="main" [depth]="1">
              <ListItemLeft><ListItemIcon><file-icon /></ListItemIcon><ListItemText>main.ts</ListItemText></ListItemLeft>
            </ListItem>
          }
        </List>
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      picked = signal<string[]>([]);
      open = signal(true);

      toggle(event: Event): void {
        event.stopPropagation(); // do not select the row while expanding/collapsing it
        this.open.update((v) => !v);
      }
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

## Options [#options]

<TypeTable
  type="{
  variant: { type: '&#x22;list-content&#x22; | &#x22;list-navigation&#x22; | &#x22;list-menu&#x22;', default: '&#x22;list-content&#x22;', description: &#x22;Set on List, propagated to every child ListItem (an item may override it locally).&#x22; },
  size: { type: '&#x22;small&#x22; | &#x22;medium&#x22;', default: '&#x22;small&#x22;', description: &#x22;Set on List, propagated to every child ListItem.&#x22; },
  value: { type: &#x22;V[]&#x22;, default: &#x22;[]&#x22;, description: &#x22;Selection model, bind with [(value)]. Always an array, even for single selection.&#x22; },
  multi: { type: &#x22;boolean&#x22;, default: &#x22;false&#x22;, description: &#x22;Enables multiple selection.&#x22; },
  selectionMode: { type: '&#x22;follow&#x22; | &#x22;explicit&#x22;', default: '&#x22;follow&#x22;', description: &#x22;follow: selection tracks keyboard focus. explicit: select only via click/Space.&#x22; },
  focusMode: { type: '&#x22;roving&#x22; | &#x22;activedescendant&#x22;', default: '&#x22;roving&#x22;', description: 'activedescendant keeps DOM focus on a host input (used by Autocomplete); the &#x22;focused&#x22; row is then exposed via data-active, not native :focus.' },
  keyboardFocused: { type: &#x22;Signal<boolean>&#x22;, description: &#x22;Read-only, via the list template reference. True while the keyboard focus (:focus-visible) is inside the list, false for a mouse click and once the focus has left.&#x22; },
}"
/>

`ListItemAction`:

<TypeTable
  type="{
  ariaLabel: { type: &#x22;string&#x22;, description: &#x22;The action's label, shown in the hover tooltip (not as aria-label): the icon is hidden from assistive technology, which reaches the action by its key.&#x22; },
  disabled: { type: &#x22;boolean&#x22;, default: &#x22;false&#x22;, description: &#x22;The key no longer triggers it, and nothing announces it any more: no aria-keyshortcuts, no linked sentence, no line.&#x22; },
  keys: { type: &#x22;readonly string[]&#x22;, default: '[&#x22;Delete&#x22;]', description: &#x22;The KeyboardEvent.key values that trigger the action. The first one names it in aria-keyshortcuts and, without shortcut, in the hint.&#x22; },
  shortcut: { type: &#x22;string&#x22;, description: 'The key\'s name, in the user\'s language, set apart as a keycap inside description. Defaults to the first key\'s short name (&#x22;Del&#x22; for Delete).' },
  description: { type: &#x22;string&#x22;, description: 'The sentence (&#x22;Press Del to delete&#x22;), linked to the row by aria-describedby and written in the row on keyboard focus. Must contain shortcut as is for it to be set apart. Without it, only aria-keyshortcuts and the bare key are given.' },
}"
/>

`trigger()` is also public: it does what a click on the icon does, unless the action is disabled. `ListItem` calls it
on the key.

`disabled`, `readonly`, `softDisabled`, `wrap`, `orientation`, `typeaheadDelay` are forwarded from
`@angular/aria/listbox`'s `Listbox` and default to whatever that package ships. `ListItem` additionally takes
`depth` (tree indentation, 20px/level) and forwards `value` (required), `disabled`, `label` from `Option`.

## Limits [#limits]

**One action per row.** `ListItem` looks for a single `ListItemAction` (the first it projects) and gives it the key.
That is a property of the component, not an omission of this page.

Projecting a second one does not fail, but only half works:

* the second icon is drawn and reacts to the **mouse** — its `(click)` fires;
* it is **unreachable from the keyboard**: the row sets `aria-keyshortcuts` and `aria-describedby` from the first
  action only, and a key press only ever triggers the first;
* each action still draws its own hint line on keyboard focus, so a focused row would advertise a key that does
  nothing.

Do not use it that way. When a row needs several actions, or an action with its own look, use a component that
can hold several focusable controls: &#x2A;*[`RowGrid`](./row-grid.mdx)** is a keyboard-navigable ARIA grid whose rows
hold any number of them — `Tab` enters the focused row and walks its controls, `Enter` activates the row.

**No editable content in a row.** A `ListItem` is a listbox `option`: ARIA forbids an interactive element inside
it, and the row takes `Delete` (and `Backspace&#x60; on a Mac) for its action whatever has the focus. A row that holds a
text field, a select or any other control is not a list row — use &#x2A;*[`RowGrid`](./row-grid.mdx)** instead.

The limit is on actions, not on keys: `keys` may list several `KeyboardEvent.key` values
(`["Delete", "Backspace"]`), all of which trigger the same action.

## Pitfalls [#pitfalls]

<Accordions>
  <Accordion title="ListItemAction's icon never receives keyboard focus, and a screen reader does not read it on mouse hover">
    `ListItemAction` renders a non-focusable `<span aria-hidden="true">`, not a `<button>` — its host `<ListItem>`
    is already a listbox `option`, and ARIA forbids an option from containing an interactive control. The label
    you pass renders in the hover tooltip, not as `aria-label`: the children of an `option` are presentational, and
    a screen reader's mouse tracking (checked with NVDA) reads nothing under the pointer in an option, whatever
    role or name the icon has. A named `role="img"` was tried and changes nothing there.

    The keyboard path is the action's key on the focused row (`keys`, `Delete` by default): `<ListItem>` sets
    `aria-keyshortcuts` from it whenever it projects a usable `ListItemAction`, and pressing the key calls the
    action's `trigger()` on your behalf — your `(click)` handler on `<ListItemAction>` still fires, unchanged.
    See [Row action and its key](#row-action-and-its-key). `ListItemExpander` is the exception in this family: it
    does render a real `<button>`, reachable by `Tab` in the usual way.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="A second ListItemAction in a row is clickable but not reachable from the keyboard">
    Only the first `ListItemAction` of a row is bound to a key: `aria-keyshortcuts`, the `aria-describedby` sentence and
    the key handling all read that one. A second one still draws and still answers to a click, which hides the
    problem from anyone testing with a mouse. See [Limits](#limits) for what to use instead.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="The key is announced but not set apart in the hint line">
    The visible line splits `description` around `shortcut` to draw the key as a keycap. If `description` does not
    contain `shortcut` exactly — a different case, a translated name that differs from the one in the sentence —
    the sentence is written as is, with no keycap. Pass the same word to both.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Backspace deletes on a Mac but not on Windows">
    That is by design, and it is the caller's choice, not the library's. `keys` is `["Delete"]` unless you say
    otherwise: Backspace in a list does not express an intent to delete on a keyboard that has a `Delete` key. A
    MacBook has none, so pass `["Delete", "Backspace"]` when `isApplePlatform()` — see
    [Name the key of a row action](#name-the-key-of-a-row-action).
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Rows overlap or misalign in a list with a custom-height template">
    `List`'s virtualizer estimates row height at a fixed value and never measures actual rendered height — keep
    rows a uniform height. This does not apply to `<aggregation-tree>`-style consumers with their own measured
    virtualizer; a plain `List` always assumes uniform rows.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="value is required on every ListItem, and it's always compared as an array">
    Even a single-selection `List` compares `value` against a `V[]` selection model — there is no scalar shortcut.
    Every `ListItem` needs its own `value`, since it is the row's identity in that array.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="A second ListItemComponent exists in @sinequa/ui, with a much smaller surface">
    `@sinequa/ui` (atomic-ui) also exports a `ListItemComponent`, but as a thinner styling-only directive
    (variants `default`/`destructive`/`primary`/`link`/`none`) with no `List` container, no slot sub-components,
    and no `@angular/aria` backing. Double-check the import path whenever `ListItem`/`ListItemComponent` is
    ambiguous — for new work, the galactik version documented here is the target.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What's next [#whats-next]

<Cards>
  <Card title="RowGrid" href="./row-grid.mdx">
    Reach for it instead of List whenever a row needs more than one focusable control.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Tabs" href="../navigation/tabs.mdx">
    Another @angular/aria-backed composite widget, for switching between panels instead of selecting rows.
  </Card>
</Cards>

# RowFeed (/docs/galactik/display/row-feed)

A WAI-ARIA feed of articles for a list of cards that grows as the user scrolls — reach for it instead of RowGrid when the list is not a table.



`RowFeed` renders a list as a WAI-ARIA feed: a `role="feed"` container of `<article>`s. A grid without headers
reads as a layout table (RGAA 5.3), so use it instead of [`RowGrid`](./row-grid.mdx) for a list of cards filled
in as the user scrolls. Article content is fully projected through an `ng-template`.

## Minimal example [#minimal-example]

<CodeSample id="row-feed-basic" title="An article-activated results feed">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component } from "@angular/core";
    import { RowFeedComponent } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    type Result = { id: string; url: string; title: string };

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [RowFeedComponent],
      template: `
        <row-feed [items]="results" [ariaLabel]="'Results'" (rowActivate)="open($event)">
          <ng-template let-item let-index="index">
            <a [href]="item.url">{{ item.title }}</a>
          </ng-template>
        </row-feed>
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      results: Result[] = [];

      open(item: Result): void {
        /* … */
      }
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

## How it works [#how-it-works]

`@angular/aria` has no feed primitive, so the keyboard lives in the component: the articles are a roving tab
stop (`tabindex` 0 on one, -1 on the others), and `↑`/`↓`, `PageUp`/`PageDown`, `Home` and `End` move from one
article to the next without wrapping. `Enter` on the article itself emits `rowActivate`. `Tab` walks the
controls inside the article as in any page, and keys pressed on those controls keep their own meaning.

Each article carries `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize` (`ariaRowCount` when the source reports a total, else
the rendered length), and the feed carries `aria-busy` while `busy` is set.

## Recipes [#recipes]

### Infinite scroll [#infinite-scroll]

<CodeSample id="row-feed-infinite" title="Loading more as focus approaches the end">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component } from "@angular/core";
    import { RowFeedComponent } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    type Result = { id: string; url: string; title: string };

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [RowFeedComponent],
      template: `
        <row-feed [items]="results" [ariaRowCount]="totalCount" [busy]="loading" (endApproached)="loadMore()">
          <ng-template let-item>{{ item.title }}</ng-template>
        </row-feed>
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      results: Result[] = [];
      totalCount = 0;
      loading = false;

      loadMore(): void {
        /* fetch the next page and append to results */
      }
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

`endApproached` fires once keyboard focus reaches the last `rowsBeforeEnd` articles, so the list keeps growing
for a keyboard user who never touches the mouse wheel.

## Options [#options]

<TypeTable
  type="{
  items: { type: &#x22;readonly T[]&#x22;, description: &#x22;Required. The articles to render.&#x22; },
  ariaLabel: { type: &#x22;string | undefined&#x22;, description: &#x22;Names the feed for assistive technology.&#x22; },
  ariaRowCount: { type: &#x22;number | null&#x22;, default: &#x22;null&#x22;, description: &#x22;Total count when items is only a partial page. Leave unset for a fully-loaded list.&#x22; },
  busy: { type: &#x22;boolean&#x22;, default: &#x22;false&#x22;, description: &#x22;More articles are loading (aria-busy).&#x22; },
  trackBy: { type: &#x22;(item: T, index: number) => unknown&#x22;, default: &#x22;(_, index) => index&#x22;, description: &#x22;Track function for the @for loop.&#x22; },
  rowsBeforeEnd: { type: &#x22;number&#x22;, default: &#x22;2&#x22;, description: &#x22;How many articles from the end a focus move starts requesting more via endApproached.&#x22; },
  gridClass: { type: &#x22;string&#x22;, default: '&#x22;gap-(--spacing-sm)&#x22;', description: &#x22;Spacing between articles.&#x22; },
  cellClass: { type: &#x22;string&#x22;, default: '&#x22;rounded-(--radius-lg)&#x22;', description: &#x22;Shape of an article.&#x22; },
}"
/>

## What's next [#whats-next]

<Cards>
  <Card title="RowGrid" href="./row-grid.mdx">
    The ARIA grid, for rows that really are tabular.
  </Card>
</Cards>

# RowGrid (/docs/galactik/display/row-grid)

A keyboard-navigable ARIA grid shell for a list of rows that hold more than one focusable control — reach for it instead of List/ListItem in that case.



`RowGrid` is a keyboard-navigable ARIA grid shell for a list of rows: `↑`/`↓` walk the rows, `Tab` enters the
focused row's own controls, `Enter` activates the row. Row content is fully projected, so it fits any row
shape a consumer needs. Reach for it instead of [`List`](./list.mdx)/`ListItem` whenever a row holds more than
one focusable control — a listbox `option` cannot contain one at all.

## Minimal example [#minimal-example]

<CodeSample id="row-grid-basic" title="A row-activated results grid">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component } from "@angular/core";
    import { RowGridComponent } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    type Result = { id: string; url: string; title: string };

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [RowGridComponent],
      template: `
        <row-grid [items]="results" [ariaLabel]="'Results'" (rowActivate)="open($event)">
          <ng-template let-item let-index="index">
            <a [href]="item.url">{{ item.title }}</a>
          </ng-template>
        </row-grid>
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      results: Result[] = [];

      open(item: Result): void {
        /* … */
      }
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

## How it works [#how-it-works]

Roles, keyboard navigation and the reflected state come entirely from `@angular/aria/grid`'s
`Grid`/`GridRow`/`GridCell` — `RowGrid` renders no ARIA behavior of its own, only the shell around it and its
two outputs.

<Mermaid
  chart="flowchart TD
    RowGrid[RowGridComponent] -- &#x22;renders&#x22; --> Row[ngGridRow]
    Row -- &#x22;renders&#x22; --> Cell[ngGridCell]
    Cell -- &#x22;ng-template outlet&#x22; --> Content[Caller-projected row content]
    Cell -- &#x22;keydown.enter&#x22; --> RowGrid
    RowGrid -- &#x22;rowActivate(item)&#x22; --> Caller
    RowGrid -- &#x22;focusin, near the end&#x22; --> RowGrid
    RowGrid -- &#x22;endApproached()&#x22; --> Caller"
/>

`rowActivate` fires on `Enter` because the interactive cell sits above the projected content in the DOM.
`endApproached` fires once keyboard focus reaches the last `rowsBeforeEnd` rows, so an infinite-scroll list can
keep growing for a keyboard user who never touches the mouse wheel.

## Recipes [#recipes]

### Infinite scroll [#infinite-scroll]

<CodeSample id="row-grid-infinite" title="Loading more as focus approaches the end">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component } from "@angular/core";
    import { RowGridComponent } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    type Result = { id: string; url: string; title: string };

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [RowGridComponent],
      template: `
        <row-grid [items]="results" [ariaRowCount]="totalCount" (endApproached)="loadMore()">
          <ng-template let-item>{{ item.title }}</ng-template>
        </row-grid>
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      results: Result[] = [];
      totalCount = 0;

      loadMore(): void {
        /* fetch the next page and append to results */
      }
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

## Options [#options]

<TypeTable
  type="{
  items: { type: &#x22;readonly T[]&#x22;, description: &#x22;Required. The rows to render.&#x22; },
  ariaLabel: { type: &#x22;string | undefined&#x22;, description: &#x22;Names the grid for assistive technology.&#x22; },
  ariaRowCount: { type: &#x22;number | null&#x22;, default: &#x22;null&#x22;, description: &#x22;Total row count when items is only a partial page. Leave unset for a fully-loaded list.&#x22; },
  trackBy: { type: &#x22;(item: T, index: number) => unknown&#x22;, default: &#x22;(_, index) => index&#x22;, description: &#x22;Track function for the @for loop.&#x22; },
  rowsBeforeEnd: { type: &#x22;number&#x22;, default: &#x22;2&#x22;, description: &#x22;How many rows from the end a keyboard focus move starts requesting more via endApproached.&#x22; },
  gridClass: { type: &#x22;string&#x22;, default: '&#x22;gap-(--spacing-sm)&#x22;', description: &#x22;Spacing between rows.&#x22; },
  cellClass: { type: &#x22;string&#x22;, default: '&#x22;rounded-(--radius-lg)&#x22;', description: &#x22;Shape of a row's cell.&#x22; },
}"
/>

## Pitfalls [#pitfalls]

<Accordions>
  <Accordion title="ArrowUp on the first row jumps to the last one, unexpectedly">
    It should not — `RowGrid` sets `rowWrap="nowrap"` deliberately: wrapping would send a keyboard user on a
    pointless trip to the far end of an infinitely-scrolling list. If you see wrapping, check that no surrounding
    code is overriding the grid's wrap behavior.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What's next [#whats-next]

<Cards>
  <Card title="List" href="./list.mdx">
    The selection-oriented alternative, for rows without their own focusable controls.
  </Card>

  <Card title="RowFeed" href="./row-feed.mdx">
    The WAI-ARIA feed, for a list of cards that is not a table.
  </Card>
</Cards>

# Tag (/docs/galactik/display/tag)

A static, read-only chip for categorizing content — a document type, an applied filter shown for reference, a status label.



`Tag` categorizes content read-only — a document type, an applied filter shown for reference, a status label.
It is a bare directive with no template: it only contributes host classes to whichever tag you write it on,
projecting its content as-is.

## Minimal example [#minimal-example]

<CodeSample id="tag-basic" title="A single tag">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component } from "@angular/core";
    import { TagComponent } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [TagComponent],
      template: `<tag variant="primary" scheme="sage">Document</tag>`,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {}
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

## How it works [#how-it-works]

`variant` (`primary` soft fill / `secondary` outline) is crossed with `scheme` (12 semantic palettes). Having
no template means a `Tag` composes with anything projected inside it — plain text, or an icon alongside a
label, sized automatically through the `.tag-icon` slot class:

<CodeSample id="tag-icon" title="Tag with an icon">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component } from "@angular/core";
    import { TagComponent, CircleCheckIcon } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [TagComponent, CircleCheckIcon],
      template: `
        <tag variant="primary" scheme="success" size="sm">
          <CircleCheckIcon class="tag-icon" />
          Verified
        </tag>
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {}
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

### Removable tags [#removable-tags]

A tag the user can take away carries a `tag-remove` after its label: a real `<button>` (Tab to reach it, Enter or Space
to activate it) named after the tag, with an `removed` event.

<CodeSample id="tag-removable" title="A list of removable tags">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component, signal } from "@angular/core";
    import { TagComponent, TagRemoveComponent } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [TagComponent, TagRemoveComponent],
      template: `
        @for (tag of tags(); track tag) {
          <tag scheme="grey" size="xs">
            {{ tag }}
            <tag-remove [aria-label]="'Remove ' + tag" (removed)="remove(tag)" />
          </tag>
        }
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      protected readonly tags = signal(["design", "angular", "tokens"]);

      protected remove(tag: string) {
        this.tags.update(tags => tags.filter(t => t !== tag));
      }
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

`TagInput`, the principal picker's chips and `Autocomplete`'s chips all use it. It is an element with its own button, not an
attribute on yours: a component that imports `ButtonComponent` (which matches every `button` of its template) would
otherwise restyle it.

## Options [#options]

<TypeTable
  type="{
  variant: { type: '&#x22;primary&#x22; | &#x22;secondary&#x22;', default: '&#x22;primary&#x22;', description: &#x22;primary = soft/tinted fill; secondary = transparent background with a colored outline.&#x22; },
  scheme: { type: '&#x22;sage&#x22; | &#x22;almond&#x22; | &#x22;pink&#x22; | &#x22;grey&#x22; | &#x22;yellow&#x22; | &#x22;cherry&#x22; | &#x22;indigo&#x22; | &#x22;cyan&#x22; | &#x22;success&#x22; | &#x22;warning&#x22; | &#x22;info&#x22; | &#x22;error&#x22;', default: '&#x22;sage&#x22;', description: &#x22;Semantic color palette.&#x22; },
  size: { type: '&#x22;xs&#x22; | &#x22;sm&#x22; | &#x22;md&#x22;', default: '&#x22;md&#x22;', description: &#x22;Controls padding, radius, text size and the .tag-icon slot size. xsmall/small/medium are accepted aliases, kept for BEM parity — prefer the short forms.&#x22; },
}"
/>

`<tag-remove>`:

<TypeTable
  type="{
  &#x22;aria-label&#x22;: { type: &#x22;string&#x22;, description: &#x22;Required. What the button removes (\&#x22;Remove design\&#x22;): an icon alone names nothing. Nothing in the library translates, so pass it translated and bind it as [aria-label].&#x22; },
  disabled: { type: &#x22;boolean&#x22;, default: &#x22;false&#x22;, description: &#x22;The button stays in place and removes nothing.&#x22; },
  removed: { type: &#x22;void&#x22;, description: &#x22;Output. Fires on a click, Enter or Space. The click does not bubble, so a handler on the field around the tags is not triggered.&#x22; },
}"
/>

## Pitfalls [#pitfalls]

<Accordions>
  <Accordion title="A removable/dismissible tag list doesn't build on Tag alone">
    `Tag` has no click handler, no `disabled` state, and no built-in remove/close button — it is read-only by
    design. For a removable tag list backed by search/selection state, reach for `Autocomplete`, which renders its
    applied values as `Tag`s internally and exposes the removal outputs; don't try to bolt dismiss behavior onto a
    bare `Tag`.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Tag and Badge's variant values aren't interchangeable">
    `Tag` uses `variant` itself for solid/outline styling (`primary`/`secondary`) and has no separate `fill`
    input. `Badge` (see [Badge](./badge.mdx)) instead uses `variant` for its icon/number discriminator and a
    separate `fill` for solid/tonal styling. The two components' `variant` values name unrelated things.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What's next [#whats-next]

<Cards>
  <Card title="Badge" href="./badge.mdx">
    A pastille apposed on another element — a counter or a status icon — rather than an inline chip.
  </Card>

  <Card title="List" href="./list.mdx">
    Render rows that might carry a Tag as a status column, alongside an icon and a label.
  </Card>
</Cards>

# BreakpointObserverService (/docs/galactik/integration/breakpoint-observer)

Answer one question as a signal — is the viewport narrower than the md breakpoint? — for structural choices CSS cannot express.



`BreakpointObserverService` answers one question as a signal: is the viewport narrower than the `md`
breakpoint (768px)? It exists for the cases CSS cannot express — choosing a component (a sheet instead of a
side panel), a placement (`bottom-start` instead of `left-start`), a size input.

<Callout title="Prefer a Tailwind md: variant when you can">
  Anything that is purely a matter of layout belongs in a Tailwind `md:` variant instead: the CSS costs nothing
  at runtime, needs no injection, and cannot fall out of sync with the service.
</Callout>

## Minimal example [#minimal-example]

<CodeSample id="breakpoint-observer-basic" title="Choosing a component based on viewport width">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component, computed, inject } from "@angular/core";
    import { BreakpointObserverService } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      template: `
        @if (breakpoints.isMobile()) {
          <sheet-previewer [record]="record()" />
        } @else {
          <preview-column [record]="record()" />
        }
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      protected readonly breakpoints = inject(BreakpointObserverService);
      protected readonly menuPlacement = computed(() => (this.breakpoints.isMobile() ? "bottom-start" : "left-start"));
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

## How it works [#how-it-works]

The service is backed by `matchMedia`, observing `(width < 768px)` — the exact negation of Tailwind's `md`, so
the signal and the CSS always agree at every width. It reacts to a resize with no `resize` listener of its
own, removes its listener when the injector is destroyed, and is inert under server-side rendering (no
`window` access — the signal stays `false`).

The viewport is measured in the constructor, not in an `afterNextRender` callback, so a consumer that injects
the service and reads `isMobile()` during change detection — a `computed`, a template expression — gets the
real answer straight away, with no render needed first.

## Options [#options]

<TypeTable
  type="{
  isMobile: { type: &#x22;Signal<boolean>&#x22;, description: &#x22;true while the viewport is narrower than 768px.&#x22; },
  isTouch: { type: &#x22;Signal<boolean>&#x22;, description: &#x22;true while the primary pointer is a finger (pointer coarse): phones and tablets, whatever their width.&#x22; },
  isLandscape: { type: &#x22;Signal<boolean>&#x22;, description: &#x22;true while the viewport is wider than tall.&#x22; },
}"
/>

`isTouch` is the answer to "can the user hover?": an iPad in landscape is wider than 768px, so `isMobile()` is `false`
there, yet nothing hovers. Use it for hover-only actions, for the size of a target and for keyboard hints.

## Hiding the focus rings on a touch screen [#hiding-the-focus-rings-on-a-touch-screen]

`provideInputModality()` starts an `InputModalityService` that tells how the page is being driven — `modality()` is
`"pointer"`, `"touch"` or `"keyboard"` — and, while it is `"touch"`, sets `--stroke-focus` to `transparent` on `<html>`.
Every galactik ring is painted with that variable, so a tap on a field no longer leaves a ring that means nothing to someone
without a keyboard. A navigation key (`Tab`, the arrows, `Home`, `End`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`, `Escape`), or any key pressed with Ctrl, Cmd or Option (a shortcut of the application: the on-screen keyboard has no such key), gives the rings
back, which a tablet with a keyboard attached does at its first `Tab`; the on-screen keyboard has none of those keys, so
typing in a field never brings them back. `data-input-modality` is written on `<html>` for your own CSS.

## Pitfalls [#pitfalls]

<Accordions>
  <Accordion title="A unit test depending on the breakpoint can't be driven to the mobile state">
    `matchMedia` is not driveable in JSDOM — it matches nothing and cannot be told to change. Provide the service
    instead of trying to steer the real one:

    ```ts title="sample.spec.ts" partial
    TestBed.configureTestingModule({
      providers: [{ provide: BreakpointObserverService, useValue: { isMobile: signal(true) } }],
    });
    ```
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What's next [#whats-next]

<Cards>
  <Card title="Sidebar" href="../navigation/sidebar.mdx">
    The component that reaches for this service to decide when to become a mobile drawer.
  </Card>
</Cards>

# Layout (/docs/galactik/layout)

Panel and list layout — ResizablePanelGroup, ResizablePanel, ResizableHandle, SortableDirective, SwipeAction — for user-resizable panels, user-reorderable lists and rows a finger swipes.



Lay a row or column of panels out with a boundary the user can drag or arrow — the split view a filters panel
and a results panel, or an editor and a preview, typically need — let the user reorder the items of a list, and give a touch screen the swipe that stands in for a hover action.

  </Card>

# Resizable (/docs/galactik/layout/resizable)

Lay a row or column of panels out and let the user move the boundary between two of them, by dragging or by arrowing the handle.



`ResizablePanelGroup` lays a row (or column) of panels out and lets the user move the boundary between two of
them, by dragging the handle or by arrowing it. Three components work together: `ResizablePanelGroup` (the
flex container and single owner of the sizes), `ResizablePanel` (one region, sized as a share of the group)
and `ResizableHandle` (the divider, focusable and draggable).

<Callout title="Concept — percentages, not pixels">
  Sizes are percentages of the group, never pixels — that is what makes a layout survive a window resize. The
  group normalizes whatever `defaultSize`s you give so they sum to 100.
</Callout>

## Minimal example [#minimal-example]

The group takes the full size of its parent (`size-full`), so it needs a parent with a height — one in a
plain `<div>` with no height collapses.

<CodeSample id="resizable-basic" title="Two panels, side by side">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component } from "@angular/core";
    import { ResizableHandleComponent, ResizablePanelComponent, ResizablePanelGroupComponent } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [ResizablePanelGroupComponent, ResizablePanelComponent, ResizableHandleComponent],
      template: `
        <div class="h-96">
          <resizable-panel-group direction="horizontal">
            <resizable-panel [defaultSize]="30" [minSize]="20">Filters</resizable-panel>
            <resizable-handle [withHandle]="true" aria-label="Resize the filters panel" />
            <resizable-panel [defaultSize]="70">Results</resizable-panel>
          </resizable-panel-group>
        </div>
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {}
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

## How it works [#how-it-works]

`minSize`/`maxSize` per panel are honoured by both the pointer and the keyboard — what one panel refuses to
take, its neighbour keeps, so the total always stays at 100%. The handle implements the ARIA
[window-splitter](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/windowsplitter/) pattern: `role="separator"`,
`aria-orientation` (the orientation of the *line*, not of the group — a separator between side-by-side panels
is vertical), and `aria-valuenow`/`valuemin`/`valuemax` bounded by the panel before it. Arrow keys move the
focused handle by 10% of the group, along the axis the group's `direction` implies — a resize is therefore
fully reachable without a pointer (WCAG 2.1.1). Dragging uses pointer events with pointer capture, so the drag
follows the pointer far outside the handle with no window-level listener, and a full-page overlay during the
drag keeps an `<iframe>` in a panel from swallowing the pointer.

## Recipes [#recipes]

### Remembering the layout [#remembering-the-layout]

Give the group an `autoSaveId` and the layout is remembered in `localStorage`, under the key
`resizable-panel:<autoSaveId>` — restored on the next visit, but only if the group still has the same number
of panels; otherwise the panels' own `defaultSize`s are the better answer.

```html
<resizable-panel-group direction="horizontal" autoSaveId="search-results">…</resizable-panel-group>
```

### Driving the layout from the outside [#driving-the-layout-from-the-outside]

<CodeSample id="resizable-external" title="Reading and resetting the layout from a button">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component, signal } from "@angular/core";
    import { ResizableHandleComponent, ResizablePanelComponent, ResizablePanelGroupComponent } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [ResizablePanelGroupComponent, ResizablePanelComponent, ResizableHandleComponent],
      template: `
        <resizable-panel-group #group="resizablePanelGroup" direction="horizontal" (layout)="sizes.set($event)">
          <resizable-panel [defaultSize]="50">Left</resizable-panel>
          <resizable-handle [withHandle]="true" aria-label="Resize panels" />
          <resizable-panel [defaultSize]="50">Right</resizable-panel>
        </resizable-panel-group>
        <button type="button" (click)="group.setLayout([50, 50])">Reset</button>
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      readonly sizes = signal<number[]>([]);
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

`setLayout()` is ignored unless the array covers exactly the panels present — a partial layout would leave the
group summing to something other than 100%.

## Options [#options]

<TypeTable
  type="{
  direction: { type: '&#x22;horizontal&#x22; | &#x22;vertical&#x22;', default: '&#x22;horizontal&#x22;', description: &#x22;Axis the panels are laid out along.&#x22; },
  autoSaveId: { type: &#x22;string | undefined&#x22;, description: &#x22;Key the layout is persisted under. Without it, nothing is stored.&#x22; },
}"
/>

### `ResizablePanel` [#resizablepanel]

<TypeTable
  type="{
  id: { type: &#x22;string&#x22;, default: '&#x22;resizable-panel-<n>&#x22;', description: &#x22;Written to the DOM — what the handle points at with aria-controls.&#x22; },
  defaultSize: { type: &#x22;number&#x22;, default: &#x22;50&#x22;, description: &#x22;Share before any resize, in percent. Normalized across siblings.&#x22; },
  minSize: { type: &#x22;number&#x22;, default: &#x22;0&#x22;, description: &#x22;Lower bound, in percent.&#x22; },
  maxSize: { type: &#x22;number&#x22;, default: &#x22;100&#x22;, description: &#x22;Upper bound, in percent.&#x22; },
}"
/>

### `ResizableHandle` [#resizablehandle]

<TypeTable
  type="{
  withHandle: { type: &#x22;boolean&#x22;, default: &#x22;false&#x22;, description: &#x22;Shows the grip pill on the line.&#x22; },
  &#x22;aria-label&#x22;: { type: &#x22;string&#x22;, default: '&#x22;Resize panels&#x22;', description: &#x22;Accessible name of the separator. Override per handle when a group has several.&#x22; },
}"
/>

## Pitfalls [#pitfalls]

<Accordions>
  <Accordion title="Dragging a handle does nothing">
    A group with no measurable size (a hidden route, `display: none`) cannot turn a pointer move into a
    percentage, and the drag is simply ignored until the group has a size again. Check that the group's parent
    actually has a height — a bare `<div>` with no height collapses the whole group to zero.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Two adjacent handles seem to control the wrong panels">
    One handle sits between every two panels, in document order — the group pairs the handle at index *i* with
    the panels at index *i* and *i+1*. A handle placed elsewhere in the projected content resizes nothing.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="A screen-reader user hears the same 'Resize panels' announced twice">
    That is the default `aria-label`, shared by every handle. Give each handle its own `aria-label` whenever a
    group has more than one.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="layout fires far more often than expected, and a heavy handler stutters the drag">
    `layout` fires on every pointer move during a drag, not only when it settles. Persist through `autoSaveId`
    instead of a manual handler, or debounce anything expensive you attach to it directly.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What's next [#whats-next]

<Cards>
  <Card title="Sidebar" href="../navigation/sidebar.mdx">
    Another panel-composition component, collapsible rather than resizable.
  </Card>
</Cards>

# Sortable (/docs/galactik/layout/sortable)

Let the user reorder a list by dragging its items, or from the keyboard with Alt and the arrow keys, with the browser's own drag and drop.



`SortableDirective` (`[sortable]`) makes the items of a list reorderable by drag and drop, and from the keyboard with
<kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd>. `SortableItemDirective` (`[sortableItem]`) marks each element. The
directive owns the gesture, not the data: it reports the new order through `(reorder)`, and the consumer keeps — and
saves — the list.

<Callout title="Concept — the order shown, and the order given">
  `sortable.items()` is the order **shown**: the list you gave, or, while an item is dragged, the order a drop would
  give. Render from it, not from your own list, and the other items make room for the dragged one as the pointer moves.
  The list you gave only changes when you adopt what `(reorder)` reports.
</Callout>

## Minimal example [#minimal-example]

<CodeSample id="sortable-basic" title="A list of steps the user reorders">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component, signal } from "@angular/core";
    import { SortableDirective, SortableItemDirective } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [SortableDirective, SortableItemDirective],
      template: `
        <ul [sortable]="steps()" #sortable="sortable" (reorder)="steps.set($event)">
          @for (step of sortable.items(); track step) {
            <li
              [sortableItem]="step"
              tabindex="0"
              class="data-dragging:border-dashed data-dragging:*:invisible">
              {{ step }}
            </li>
          }
        </ul>
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      protected readonly steps = signal(["Collect", "Index", "Search", "Review"]);
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

Track the `@for` by the item itself: the elements are moved, not recreated, which is what lets them slide and keep
the keyboard focus. The element being dragged carries `data-dragging` — style it as the placeholder of the slot the
item will land in (`data-dragging:border-dashed`, and `data-dragging:*:invisible` to empty it).

## How it works [#how-it-works]

<Mermaid
  chart="sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant I as sortableItem
    participant S as sortable
    participant C as Consumer
    U->>I: dragstart
    I->>S: startDrag
    S->>S: build the tilted copy, hide the browser's image
    U->>I: dragover another item
    I->>S: dragOver
    S->>S: items() becomes the preview, the others slide
    U->>I: drop
    S->>C: reorder with the new order
    C->>S: sortable input receives the new order
    S->>S: the copy settles in its slot, the preview is dropped"
/>

The browser's own drag image is made invisible, and the copy that follows the pointer is drawn by the directive: a
clone of the dragged element, tilted by 3° (and by −3° when the pointer goes up), lifted by a shadow, and placed in
the top layer with the `popover` attribute — so it stays above a popover that hosts the list. A browser may flatten
the transform of a native drag image; a clone it does not draw cannot be flattened.

A drag that is abandoned — dropped outside the list, <kbd>Esc</kbd> — puts the items back, sends the copy home, and
emits nothing. With reduced motion requested (`prefers-reduced-motion`), the items and the copy do not animate.

## Recipes [#recipes]

### Telling a screen reader about a move [#telling-a-screen-reader-about-a-move]

The library translates nothing, so a keyboard move is silent until `sortableAnnounce` provides the sentence. It is
read through a live region the directive creates on the first move.

<CodeSample id="sortable-announce" title="Announce a keyboard move">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component, signal } from "@angular/core";
    import { SortableDirective, SortableItemDirective } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [SortableDirective, SortableItemDirective],
      template: `
        <ul [sortable]="items()" #sortable="sortable" [sortableAnnounce]="announce" (reorder)="items.set($event)">
          @for (item of sortable.items(); track item) {
            <li [sortableItem]="item" tabindex="0">{{ item }}</li>
          }
        </ul>
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      protected readonly items = signal(["Security", "Performance", "Accessibility"]);

      protected readonly announce = (item: string, position: number, total: number) =>
        `${item} moved to position ${position} of ${total}`;
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

### Saving the order [#saving-the-order]

Adopt the new order at once and put the previous one back if the request fails: the list shown follows the list
you gave, so a drop keeps its result on screen while the request is in flight.

<CodeSample id="sortable-save" title="An optimistic save">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component, signal } from "@angular/core";
    import { SortableDirective, SortableItemDirective } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [SortableDirective, SortableItemDirective],
      template: `
        <ul [sortable]="items()" #sortable="sortable" (reorder)="save($event)">
          @for (item of sortable.items(); track item) {
            <li [sortableItem]="item" tabindex="0">{{ item }}</li>
          }
        </ul>
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      protected readonly items = signal(["Draft", "Review", "Approved"]);

      protected async save(next: string[]): Promise<void> {
        const previous = this.items();
        this.items.set(next);
        try {
          await fetch("/api/order", { method: "PUT", body: JSON.stringify(next) });
        } catch {
          this.items.set(previous);
        }
      }
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

### Turning it off [#turning-it-off]

`sortableDisabled` removes `draggable` and ignores the shortcut — for a list the user may not reorder right now.

<CodeSample id="sortable-disabled" title="A locked list">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component, signal } from "@angular/core";
    import { SortableDirective, SortableItemDirective } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [SortableDirective, SortableItemDirective],
      template: `
        <ul [sortable]="items()" #sortable="sortable" [sortableDisabled]="locked()" (reorder)="items.set($event)">
          @for (item of sortable.items(); track item) {
            <li [sortableItem]="item" tabindex="0">{{ item }}</li>
          }
        </ul>
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      protected readonly items = signal(["Draft", "Review", "Approved"]);
      protected readonly locked = signal(true);
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

### Keeping one item in place [#keeping-one-item-in-place]

`sortableItemDisabled` keeps one item from being moved, by the pointer or the keyboard, while the others stay free.
They may still be dropped before or after it: a disabled item is not moved by the user, but its position shifts to
make room. It carries `data-disabled`: style it so that it is easy to tell from the others — a flat neutral
background, muted text, no hover, and no handle if the items have one.

<CodeSample id="sortable-item-disabled" title="One fixed item among free ones">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component, signal } from "@angular/core";
    import { SortableDirective, SortableItemDirective } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [SortableDirective, SortableItemDirective],
      template: `
        <ul [sortable]="folders()" #sortable="sortable" (reorder)="folders.set($event)">
          @for (folder of sortable.items(); track folder) {
            <li
              [sortableItem]="folder"
              [sortableItemDisabled]="folder === 'Inbox'"
              tabindex="0"
              class="group not-data-disabled:hover:bg-(--bg-primary-lighter) data-disabled:cursor-default data-disabled:bg-(--bg-neutral-base) data-disabled:text-(--font-neutral-muted)">
              {{ folder }}
            </li>
          }
        </ul>
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      protected readonly folders = signal(["Inbox", "Projects", "Archive", "Drafts"]);
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

## Options [#options]

### SortableDirective [#sortabledirective]

<TypeTable
  type="{
  sortable: { type: &#x22;readonly T[]&#x22;, description: &#x22;The items, in their current order. Required.&#x22; },
  sortableDisabled: { type: &#x22;boolean&#x22;, default: &#x22;false&#x22;, description: &#x22;Turns the reordering off: nothing is draggable, the shortcut does nothing.&#x22; },
  sortableAnnounce: { type: &#x22;(item: T, position: number, total: number) => string&#x22;, description: &#x22;The sentence read to screen readers after a keyboard move. Without it, a move is silent.&#x22; },
  reorder: { type: &#x22;OutputEmitterRef<T[]>&#x22;, description: &#x22;The new order, on a drop that changes it and on a keyboard move. Never for an abandoned drag.&#x22; },
  items: { type: &#x22;Signal<readonly T[]>&#x22;, description: &#x22;The order to render: the given one, or the preview of the drop while an item is dragged.&#x22; },
  dragged: { type: &#x22;Signal<T | undefined>&#x22;, description: &#x22;The item being dragged, if any.&#x22; },
}"
/>

### SortableItemDirective [#sortableitemdirective]

<TypeTable
  type="{
  sortableItem: { type: &#x22;T&#x22;, description: &#x22;The item this element stands for — the same value as in the list given to sortable. Required.&#x22; },
  sortableItemDisabled: { type: &#x22;boolean&#x22;, default: &#x22;false&#x22;, description: &#x22;Keeps this item from being moved, by the pointer or the keyboard. The others stay free, and may be dropped before or after it.&#x22; },
}"
/>

The element also gets `draggable="true"` and `aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+ArrowUp Alt+ArrowDown"` (neither when it is disabled, or the list is), `data-dragging` while it is the one being dragged, and `data-disabled` when it cannot be moved.

## Pitfalls [#pitfalls]

<Accordions>
  <Accordion title="The items jump instead of sliding, or lose the focus after a keyboard move">
    The `@for` is tracked by something that changes when the order does (`track $index`, or a new object per render).
    The directive moves existing elements; give `track` the item itself.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="The dropped item snaps back for an instant">
    The consumer keeps its own copy of the list and adopts the new order late (after a request). Adopt it in the
    `(reorder)` handler, synchronously, and roll it back on failure — the list shown follows the list given.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Alt + arrow does nothing inside a field of the item">
    Deliberate. The shortcut only works while the item itself has the focus: Alt + arrows inside an input or a button
    of the item are theirs.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Nothing can be reordered on a touch screen">
    A browser that does not start a native drag on touch leaves no way to reorder: the keyboard shortcut is the only
    alternative, and it is not available there either. Offer another control (move up and down buttons) where touch
    matters.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What's next [#whats-next]

<Cards>
  <Card title="Resizable" href="./resizable.mdx">
    Panels whose boundary the user moves by dragging or arrowing a handle.
  </Card>
</Cards>

# SwipeAction (/docs/galactik/layout/swipe-action)

Reveal an action when the user drags a row sideways with a finger — the touch counterpart of an action that only shows on hover.



`<SwipeAction>` wraps a row and lets a finger drag it to the left or to the right: a coloured layer with the action
appears under it, and releasing the row past a threshold triggers the action (the iOS Mail gesture). It is what stands in
for a hover-only action on a touch screen, where nothing hovers.

<Callout title="A swipe is a shortcut, never the only way">
  A hidden gesture does not exist for a screen reader or a switch user. Keep the action reachable by a visible button
  (`pointer-coarse:sr-only` once the swipe replaces it for a sighted finger), and give the row its keyboard path as before.
</Callout>

## Minimal example [#minimal-example]

<CodeSample id="swipe-action-basic" title="A row deleted by a swipe to the left">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component, signal } from "@angular/core";
    import { SwipeActionComponent, XMarkIcon } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [SwipeActionComponent, XMarkIcon],
      template: `
        @for (item of items(); track item) {
          <SwipeAction endEnabled (swipedEnd)="remove(item)" contentClass="flex items-center bg-(--layer-page-layer) p-3">
            <span swipeActionEnd><XMarkIcon /> Delete</span>
            <span class="flex-1">{{ item }}</span>
            <button type="button" class="pointer-coarse:sr-only" (click)="remove(item)">Delete</button>
          </SwipeAction>
        }
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      protected readonly items = signal(["Quarterly results", "Hiring plan", "Roadmap"]);

      protected remove(item: string): void {
        this.items.update(list => list.filter(entry => entry !== item));
      }
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

## How it works [#how-it-works]

<Mermaid
  chart="sequenceDiagram
    participant F as Finger
    participant S as SwipeAction
    participant C as Consumer
    F->>S: pointerdown
    F->>S: pointermove, 8px
    S->>S: horizontal or vertical?
    Note over S: vertical, the browser scrolls and the gesture ends
    S->>S: horizontal, capture the pointer, the row follows
    F->>S: pointerup past the threshold
    S->>C: swipedEnd or swipedStart
    S->>S: the row slides back, the click of the release is swallowed"
/>

* **Only a finger or a pen** drives it (`pointerType` other than `mouse`): with a mouse the row keeps its hover actions,
  and selecting text by dragging is untouched.
* **A vertical drag is the browser's.** The host sets `touch-action: pan-y`, so a list still scrolls, and a gesture that
  starts vertical is dropped for good.
* **The layers are as wide as the space the drag frees**, pinned to their edge: they never sit behind the row, so the
  row needs no opaque background of its own to hide them.
* **A direction that is not enabled does not move at all** — the row does not give way to the left if only `startEnabled`
  is set.
* **The release does not click.** The click the browser fires under the finger after a drag is swallowed, so a swipe never
  opens the row it deletes.
* Past the threshold the layer turns solid (white text on the full colour of its tone) and the action grows a little: the layer carries `data-armed`, so a release now triggers it. Pulling back under the threshold disarms it.
* The row slides back after every release, whether or not it triggered: the consumer decides what the action does (remove
  the item, toggle a favourite) and the row is re-rendered from there.

## Recipes [#recipes]

### Two actions, one per direction [#two-actions-one-per-direction]

<CodeSample id="swipe-action-both" title="Favourite to the right, delete to the left">
  <Lang value="angular">
    ```ts title="sample.component.ts"
    import { Component } from "@angular/core";
    import { StarIcon, SwipeActionComponent, XMarkIcon } from "@sinequa/galactik";

    @Component({
      selector: "sample-component",
      imports: [SwipeActionComponent, StarIcon, XMarkIcon],
      template: `
        <SwipeAction
          startEnabled
          endEnabled
          startTone="warning"
          endTone="error"
          (swipedStart)="favorite()"
          (swipedEnd)="remove()"
          contentClass="flex items-center bg-(--layer-page-layer) p-3">
          <span swipeActionStart><StarIcon /> Favourite</span>
          <span swipeActionEnd><XMarkIcon /> Delete</span>
          <span>Quarterly results</span>
        </SwipeAction>
      `,
    })
    export class SampleComponent {
      protected favorite(): void {}
      protected remove(): void {}
    }
    ```
  </Lang>
</CodeSample>

By convention the **left** swipe (`end`) is the destructive one, as on iOS, and the **right** swipe (`start`) the
positive one. `startTone` / `endTone` take `success`, `warning`, `error` or `accent`, all galactik tokens.

### Only on a touch screen [#only-on-a-touch-screen]

`SwipeAction` is inert with a mouse, so it can wrap the row on every device. What changes under a finger is the visible
button, which the swipe replaces:

```html
<button class="pointer-coarse:sr-only" (click)="remove()">Delete</button>
```

Keep it in the DOM (`sr-only`), not `hidden`: a screen reader on a tablet still needs it.

### A row that must not swipe [#a-row-that-must-not-swipe]

Set `[disabled]="true"`, or leave both `*Enabled` inputs off. The host then drops `touch-action` too.

## Options [#options]

<TypeTable
  type="{
  startEnabled: { type: &#x22;boolean&#x22;, default: &#x22;false&#x22;, description: &#x22;Allows a drag to the right, which reveals the `[swipeActionStart]` slot.&#x22; },
  endEnabled: { type: &#x22;boolean&#x22;, default: &#x22;false&#x22;, description: &#x22;Allows a drag to the left, which reveals the `[swipeActionEnd]` slot.&#x22; },
  startTone: { type: &#x22;'success' | 'warning' | 'error' | 'accent'&#x22;, default: &#x22;'success'&#x22;, description: &#x22;Colour of the layer a drag to the right reveals.&#x22; },
  endTone: { type: &#x22;'success' | 'warning' | 'error' | 'accent'&#x22;, default: &#x22;'error'&#x22;, description: &#x22;Colour of the layer a drag to the left reveals.&#x22; },
  threshold: { type: &#x22;number&#x22;, default: &#x22;96&#x22;, description: &#x22;Distance in px past which releasing the row triggers the action.&#x22; },
  disabled: { type: &#x22;boolean&#x22;, default: &#x22;false&#x22;, description: &#x22;Turns the gesture off, `touch-action` included.&#x22; },
  contentClass: { type: &#x22;string&#x22;, description: &#x22;Classes of the layer that slides: the layout of the row, its hover colours, its background.&#x22; },
  class: { type: &#x22;string&#x22;, description: &#x22;Classes merged on the host.&#x22; },
  swipedStart: { type: &#x22;OutputEmitterRef<void>&#x22;, description: &#x22;The row was released past the threshold after a drag to the right.&#x22; },
  swipedEnd: { type: &#x22;OutputEmitterRef<void>&#x22;, description: &#x22;The row was released past the threshold after a drag to the left.&#x22; },
}"
/>

## Pitfalls [#pitfalls]

<Accordions>
  <Accordion title="The row slides but nothing reveals">
    The slot is projected by its attribute: `<span swipeActionEnd>` for a drag to the left, `<span swipeActionStart>` for a drag
    to the right. A slot with no matching `*Enabled` input is not rendered at all.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="A tap on the row after a swipe does nothing">
    The click that follows a drag is swallowed on purpose, for 400ms at most. If the finger left the row and no click came, the
    swallow ends by itself and the next tap is a genuine one.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="A unit test cannot drive the swipe">
    JSDOM has no layout: `clientWidth` is 0, so the row is not clamped, and `setPointerCapture` may be missing. Dispatch
    `pointerdown`, `pointermove` and `pointerup` events with `pointerType: "touch"` and assert on the emitted output.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What's next [#whats-next]

    `isTouch()` and `provideInputModality()`: how the library tells a finger from a mouse.
